newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Delta says Kanowna Belle production up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Delta says Kanowna Belle production up.

text.p: Gold miner Delta Gold Ltd said on Wednesday the Kanowna Belle mine in Western Australia reported record production in the second quarter to December 31 of 46,740 ounces, up from 39,921 ounces in the September quarter.
The increase was due to continuing high mill throughput and the treatment of a greater proportion of high-grade ore at the mine, a 50-50 joint venture with North Ltd.
The cash operating cost declined slightly to A$262 an ounce from A$264 an ounce, Delta said.
An accelerated mining plan has been adopted at the mine which will bring production forward and increase gold output for the next few years, Delta said.
Delta's share of production from Kanowna Belle and the Granny Smith mine, in which it has a 40 percent interest, totalled 46,214 ounces in the December quarter.
This compared with 46,193 ounces in the December quarter a year ago and 42,143 ounces in the September quarter.
Placer Pacific Ltd owns the remainder of Granny Smith.

In Zimbabwe, where Delta has a 33 percent stake in the Hartley Platinum mine being developed by the Broken Hill Pty Ltd Co, Delta said a pre-feasibility study was continuing at the nearby Ngezi platinum deposit.
The pre-feasibility study at Ngezi, 100 percent owned by Delta, should be completed by the end of January, it said.
